q: What is the capital of Nigeria?
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Recall Nigerian capital history
• 1914-1991: Lagos was the capital
• December 1991: Capital officially moved to Abuja
• Abuja was purpose-built as the new capital

Step 2: Identify the current capital
• Current capital = ABUJA

Step 3: Analyze options
• Option A (Lagos): FORMER capital, commercial center ✗
• Option B (Abuja): CURRENT capital ✓ Correct!
• Option C (Kano): State capital, not national ✗
• Option D (Ibadan): State capital, not national ✗

The correct answer is B) Abuja.

q: Which is the longest river in Nigeria?
exp: River Niger is the longest river in Nigeria.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Recall major Nigerian rivers
• River Niger: ~4,180 km total (longest)
• River Benue: ~1,400 km (major tributary)
• River Kaduna: Tributary of Niger
• River Ogun: Short southwestern river

Step 2: Identify the longest
• River Niger is the LONGEST
• Third longest in Africa (after Nile and Congo)

Step 3: Analyze options
• Option A (Benue): Major tributary, not longest ✗
• Option B (Niger): Longest ✓ Correct!
• Option C (Kaduna): Minor tributary ✗
• Option D (Ogun): Minor river ✗

The correct answer is B) River Niger.

q: The tropical rainforest is characterized by:
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Recall vegetation types
• Desert: Sparse vegetation, cacti, shrubs
• Rainforest: DENSE multi-layered vegetation
• Savanna: Grasses with scattered trees
• Tundra: Moss and lichens

Step 2: Understand rainforest conditions
• High rainfall (200+ cm annually)
• High temperature
• Multiple canopy layers (emergent, canopy, understory, forest floor)

Step 3: Analyze options
• Option A (Sparse): Desert ✗
• Option B (Dense multi-layered): Rainforest ✓ Correct!
• Option C (Cacti): Desert ✗
• Option D (Grasses): Savanna ✗

The correct answer is B) Dense multi-layered vegetation.

q: Which of the following is a renewable natural resource?
exp: Solar energy is renewable as it comes from the sun.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Define renewable vs non-renewable
• Renewable: Can be replenished naturally (solar, wind, water)
• Non-renewable: Finite, takes millions of years to form (fossil fuels)

Step 2: Classify options
• Coal: Fossil fuel, non-renewable ✗
• Petroleum: Fossil fuel, non-renewable ✗
• Solar energy: From sun, RENEWABLE ✓
• Natural gas: Fossil fuel, non-renewable ✗

Step 3: Understand why solar is renewable
• Sun provides continuous energy
• Will not run out for billions of years

Option A: Non-renewable ✗
Option B: Non-renewable ✗
Option C: Renewable ✓ Correct!
Option D: Non-renewable ✗

The correct answer is C) Solar energy.

q: The highest mountain in Africa is:
exp: Mount Kilimanjaro (5,895 m) is Africa's highest peak.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Recall mountain heights
• Mount Kilimanjaro: 5,895 m (Tanzania) - HIGHEST in Africa
• Mount Kenya: 5,199 m (Kenya) - Second in Africa
• Mount Everest: 8,849 m (Nepal/China) - Highest in WORLD
• Mount Cameroon: 4,040 m (Cameroon)

Step 2: Identify African mountain
• Mount Kilimanjaro is the highest IN AFRICA

Step 3: Analyze options
• Option A (Kenya): Second highest ✗
• Option B (Kilimanjaro): Highest ✓ Correct!
• Option C (Everest): In Asia, not Africa ✗
• Option D (Cameroon): Much shorter ✗

The correct answer is B) Mount Kilimanjaro.

q: The layer of the atmosphere closest to Earth's surface is:
exp: The troposphere is the lowest layer of the atmosphere.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: List atmospheric layers (bottom to top)
1. Troposphere (0-12 km) ← CLOSEST to Earth
2. Stratosphere (12-50 km) - contains ozone layer
3. Mesosphere (50-85 km) - meteors burn up
4. Thermosphere (85-600 km) - aurora occurs

Step 2: Identify the closest layer
• Troposphere is the FIRST layer
• Contains 75% of atmospheric mass
• Where all WEATHER occurs

Step 3: Analyze options
• Option A (Stratosphere): Second layer ✗
• Option B (Troposphere): First layer ✓ Correct!
• Option C (Mesosphere): Third layer ✗
• Option D (Thermosphere): Fourth layer ✗

The correct answer is B) Troposphere.

q: Which of these is NOT a main type of rock?
exp: Volcanic glass is a type of igneous rock, not a rock category.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Recall the three main rock types
1. Igneous - Formed from cooled magma/lava
2. Sedimentary - Formed from compressed sediments
3. Metamorphic - Changed by heat and pressure

Step 2: Understand volcanic glass
• Volcanic glass (obsidian) is a TYPE of igneous rock
• Forms when lava cools VERY quickly
• Not a separate rock category

Step 3: Analyze options
• Option A (Igneous): Main rock type ✓
• Option B (Sedimentary): Main rock type ✓
• Option C (Metamorphic): Main rock type ✓
• Option D (Volcanic glass): Type of igneous, NOT a category ✗ Correct answer!

The correct answer is D) Volcanic glass.

q: The largest ocean in the world is:
exp: The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean on Earth.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Recall ocean sizes (largest to smallest)
1. Pacific: 165 million km² ← LARGEST
2. Atlantic: 106 million km²
3. Indian: 70 million km²
4. Arctic: 14 million km² (smallest)

Step 2: Identify the largest
• Pacific Ocean covers ~30% of Earth's surface
• Contains deepest point (Mariana Trench)

Step 3: Analyze options
• Option A (Atlantic): Second largest ✗
• Option B (Indian): Third largest ✗
• Option C (Pacific): Largest ✓ Correct!
• Option D (Arctic): Smallest ✗

The correct answer is C) Pacific Ocean.

q: The imaginary line that divides Earth into Northern and Southern hemispheres is:
exp: The Equator divides Earth into Northern and Southern hemispheres.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Recall geographic lines
• Prime Meridian: 0° longitude, divides EAST/WEST
• Equator: 0° latitude, divides NORTH/SOUTH
• Tropic of Cancer: 23.5°N latitude
• Arctic Circle: 66.5°N latitude

Step 2: Match the description
• "Divides Northern and Southern hemispheres" = Equator

Step 3: Analyze options
• Option A (Prime Meridian): East/West division ✗
• Option B (Equator): North/South division ✓ Correct!
• Option C: Latitude line in north ✗
• Option D: Latitude line in north ✗

The correct answer is B) Equator.

q: Which country is Nigeria's western neighbor?
exp: Benin Republic borders Nigeria to the west.
ai_exp:
Step-by-Step Analysis:

Step 1: Recall Nigeria's borders
• West: BENIN REPUBLIC
• East: Cameroon
• North: Niger
• Northeast: Chad
• South: Atlantic Ocean (Gulf of Guinea)

Step 2: Identify western neighbor
• Benin Republic is to the WEST

Step 3: Analyze options
• Option A (Cameroon): Eastern border ✗
• Option B (Chad): Northeastern border ✗
• Option C (Benin): Western border ✓ Correct!
• Option D (Niger): Northern border ✗

The correct answer is C) Benin Republic.
